title: Physical change
competency: Describe physical change with everyday examples.

keywords.def: A change in physical appearance, not in chemical composition. No new substance forms.

en.text: A physical change changes how a substance looks, but not what it is made of. No new substance forms. Melting ice, grinding salt, tearing paper, making an iron bar magnetic, evaporating water, dissolving sugar and breaking a stick are physical changes.

screens.title: Torn paper
screens.ask: You tear a sheet of paper into small pieces. Is each piece still paper?
opts: No, it is a new substance
screens.after: Each piece is still paper. Only the size and shape changed: a physical change.

screens.title: 2.4 Change around us
paras: Change is happening around us all the time.
Changes are classified as physical or chemical changes.

screens.title: 2.4.1 Physical change
paras: A physical change changes the physical appearance of a substance.
It does not change the chemical composition.
A new substance is never formed.

screens.title: Common physical changes
items: Solid water becomes liquid water. Still water.
Big crystals become powder. Still salt.
The sugar is still there; evaporate the water to get it back.
Smaller pieces of the same wood.

test.text: Abebe melts butter, then lets it cool and harden again. Which is true?
